name: 500 (Sicilian)
description: 500 Sicilian is a variant of the trick-taking game 500 adapted for the 40-card Sicilian/Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs; 1-7 + Fante/Cavallo/Re). Bidding for tricks + trump suit. Misère available. Adapted scoring and hand structure for 40-card deck. First to 500 points wins. Kitty/widow for bid winner.

content.text: 500 Sicilian is a variant of the trick-taking game 500 adapted for the 40-card Sicilian/Italian deck (Coins, Cups, Swords, Clubs; 1-7 + Fante/Cavallo/Re). Bidding for tricks + trump suit. Misère available. Adapted scoring and hand structure for 40-card deck. First to 500 points wins. Kitty/widow for bid winner.

500 (Five Hundred) originated in the United States as an extension of Euchre, developed before 1900 and copyrighted by the US Playing Card Company in 1904. It became the national card game of Australia and spread to New Zealand, Canada, and elsewhere. Sicilian 500 is a regional adaptation: Italian and Sicilian players later adapted 500's bidding and trick-taking structure to the 40-card Italian deck used in local games such as Briscola and Scopa, preserving contract bidding, kitty, and first-to-500 scoring while using Italian suits and face cards (Fante, Cavallo, Re).
40 Sicilian cards: 4 suits (Coins/Cups/Swords/Clubs), 1-7 + Fante + Cavallo + Re.

items.text: Misère: Bid to lose every trick; no trump. Contract: take zero tricks; fail scores negative.
